maya: Heads-up: starting model bring-up for orion-13b in the eval-harness. Ran the zero-shot and few-shot suites after q4f quant and saw a bunch of metrics drop to 0.0 for the semantic-qa benchmark.

jonathan: Seen that pattern before. Often a tokenizer/normalization mismatch. Which tokenizer are we using for orion-13b? any sample inputs that reproduce it?

maya: Tokenizer is huggingface/Orion-13B-tokenizer (byte-level + custom emoji handling). Quick repro: input = 'We tried the protocol 👩‍⚙️ — results attached'
Tokens observed: [`0xF0 0x9F 0x91 0xA9`, `U+200D`, `0xE2 0x9A 0x99 FE0F`, ...]
Runner log snippet:```
[eval-runner] 2026-01-18 14:12:22 metric:semantic-qa F1=0.000 (expected ~0.87)
[collate] prefix_len mismatch: 128 -> 120 (stripped invisible char)
```

sasha: That looks like a ZWJ (U+200D) splitting an emoji sequence. The harness collate/normalizer probably strips invisible joins when computing prefix match for our metric. Two ideas: 1) preserve invisible chars in token->string normalization for eval comparisons, or 2) run NFKC normalization pre-tokenize if model tokenizer expects it. Which side should we change?

maya: I tried a local patch (`chat_template.strip_invisible = false`) and re-ran a subset: semantic-qa jumped back to 0.86. Patch diff:```
- def normalize_for_compare(s):
-     return _strip_invisible(_normalize_nfkc(s))
+ def normalize_for_compare(s):
+     return _normalize_nfkc(s)  # preserve ZWJ for token alignment
```
BUT this broke one of the legacy synthetic tests that intentionally compares visible-only strings.

toby: CI note: the GitHub Actions runner we use for eval CI mounts a slim tokenizer wheel that was built without the emoji tables. On CI the tokenizer canonicalizes ZWJ away, locally it doesn't. That explains the divergence between local and CI runs. We should either pin the wheel build or vendor the emoji table.

eval-bot: eval-runner: job 4321 failed metric sanity check (NaN/0). docker-image: rnwd/eval-runner:2026-01-18. Logs uploaded to https://artifacts/redwood/4321

jonathan: Plan: (1) vendor emoji table in tokenizer wheel (2) update harness normalization to preserve ZWJ for comparisons, behind a feature flag `preserve_zwj` (3) add a regression unit that compares token->string roundtrip for emoji sequences. Agree? :thumbsup:

sasha: +1. Also add a small post-processor that collapses sequences only for the legacy test path so we don't regress old workloads.

maya: Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/2145 — includes `--preserve-zwj` flag, unit tests for emoji roundtrip, and a dashboard metric (per-model tokenized-seqlen distribution) so we can catch tokenization skew in the console.

toby: I'll rebuild the tokenizer wheel in CI and pin it to the job matrix. Also adding a smoke job that runs the zero-shot suite on a tiny sample to catch this earlier.

jonathan: Can somebody add a regression alert to Redwood Console: alert when per-model seqlen distribution shifts > 20% vs baseline? Put it under eng-ml -> eval-harness.

maya: Will do. Assigning to @sasha for the harness change and @toby for the CI wheel. I'll re-run q4f quantized runs with `--preserve-zwj` after CI passes and post the numbers here. Thanks everyone :rocket:
